rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Setup 3 Turn 4 Training Cards 5 Game End Overview Manage a dog shelter whilst trying to find homes for the stray dogs you pick up. Win by scoring the most reputation points by completing training cards, finding your dogs a home, and competing for shelter commendations Setup Starting with the first player, each player picks 1 dog Then, starting with the last player, each player picks a second dog After which, all players place their first 2 dogs onto their grid Turn On your turn, you perform two actions, these can be the same or different. You can take a dog and place it in an open space in your Shelter , after which a new dog is drawn to replace it, if this was your first action this means you may take the dog that was just drawn for your second action You can take a training card into your hand , after which a new card is drawn to replace it, if this was your first action this means you may take the card that was just drawn for your second action (hand limit is 5) You can move a dog already in your shelter to an open space orthogonally or diagonally adjacent to it Training Cards In addition to your normal turn actions, you can play training cards from your hand if you have completed their requirements These cards show a configuration shape of dogs it wants the player to make on their board A beige and a dark bordered dog are single groups of one dog type each, whilst a multi-coloured dog is any dog and a cross in a space means it must be empty The medallion on the lower right shows how many points the card is worth, whilst the house on the top left shows how many dogs out of those needed to make the pattern will actually get rehomed Player can Rehome a dog wherever they like (City, Suburbs, Countryside or Foster Home) but the different areas have different conditions as to how they might score at end game e.g. the Foster Home gives 1 point per any dog Game End Once one player has played their 7th Training card, the round is completed in full and then it ends Alternatively, if somehow the group manages to run out of dogs or training cards to draw at any point, this triggers end game too After which, commendations are awarded for meeting certain conditions, multiple players can meet the same conditions if they apply and get the same rewards From this, add Training and Home points gained Whoever has the most points wins! If tied, the player who homed the most dogs wins!

[Rating: 2/10] Seems simple enough with no new mechanic. Will have other better games to play in place of this.

[Rating: 3/10] Players pick pieces and place them on their board to complete cards for points. Most points wins.

[Rating: 3.5/10] The collection of mechanisms on offer feels as if a certain popular style of game, the take and make a la Cascadia and other, was briefly analyzed and boiled down to a few categories of mechanisms (e.g., draft, varying scoring categories, personal tableau, etc.). Then one twist was added as a way to provide some modicum of differentiation. In this case, that is the pattern matching. But the pattern matching of this game pales in comparison to what is found in other titles, like Tash Kalar and Bullet. The result is a game that is painfully generic a devoid of memorable moments.

[Rating: 4/10] Edit: Lowered to a 4. Too many instances that require you to want to strategize keeping certain dogs from being rehomed to gain points really emphasized the slapped on theme and just kinda muddy up the whole experience for me.   Disappointingly open spatial puzzle that really doesn't bring much to the table. I like the idea of needing to constantly be rearranging your board as you move dogs from your puzzle to their forever home to earn you points, but the result is that the game never feels like a puzzle as much as it does just a slightly more complicated set collection/pattern matching game.

[Rating: 4/10] Played first time at Buzzin meeples in Manchester, UK.  Game is quick and has some thinky ouzzles.  only issue i have is game ends too quickly in my opinion, and highlights who took the optimal actions.
